chapter: Young players, schools and studio work
title: Sneakers at NBC and Goodman's order to change
summary: Arriving at NBC in corduroys and sneakers in 1939, Goodman sends him home to change.

story.theme_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the leader and his bands
story.community_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the perfectionist bandleader

blocks.x: I found /that in Benny Goodman's band. I came from California and we were very casual out there. I wore -- this was in '39, I wore courderoys and I didn't wear socks, I wore sneakers and a sweatshirt. So I showed up at NBC for rehearsals for the Camel show. I knew I'd wear a tux that night, and I showed up in my courderoys and my sweatshirt and my sneakers and he took one, look at them and he said, go put on a suit and tie. This is New York, it's not Santa Monica Beach.

Now, that was a little extreme, but still, you did what the leader said. I went home and I thought he had every right to tell me that, so I went home and I changed and came back to rehearsal. So from then on, I never made the mistake. That carried over for three or four more years until I got in the studios, I was careful about it.
